rulings.caseName: Collazo v. Illinois State Board of Elections
rulings.citation: Sangamon County No. 2024 CH 000032; appeal 2024 IL 130769
rulings.dateType: Signed trial-court memorandum opinion and order
rulings.court: Sangamon County Circuit Court; direct appeal to Illinois Supreme Court
rulings.judgeRole: Trial judge who signed the declaratory judgment and permanent injunction
rulings.topic: Ballot access and changing election rules during an election cycle
rulings.holding: Noll ruled that the 2024 law eliminating post-primary slating for General Assembly candidates was unconstitutional as applied to the named plaintiffs in that year's election. She barred the State Board and its members from using the change to reject those plaintiffs' nomination papers or keep their names off the November 2024 ballot.
rulings.reasoning: The plaintiffs had lost a previously available ballot-access route after the primary and could not use another statutory route. Noll applied strict scrutiny, finding the mid-cycle change severely burdened voting and ballot-access rights and that applying the change next election would be less restrictive. She also found arbitrary unequal treatment under the alternative Anderson-Burdick analysis. The injunction was expressly limited to the named plaintiffs; relief against the attorney general was denied because that office did not certify candidates.
rulings.subsequentHistory: On August 23, 2024, the Illinois Supreme Court dismissed the direct appeal because two justices recused themselves and the remaining justices could not supply the constitutionally required four votes. Its opinion says dismissal had the effect of an equal-division affirmance but no precedential value. This was not a Supreme Court majority decision endorsing Noll's reasoning, nor a ruling voiding the statute for all future elections.

sbe-8th-circuit-retain-burch-charles-h-w.name: Charles H.W. Burch
sbe-8th-circuit-retain-burch-charles-h-w.searchScope: Official Illinois Courts all-year index search for Burch; 158 full-text hits. Verified the Calhoun County judge in the Green opinion caption; excluded similarly named judges and cases in which Charles Burch was a party or lawyer.

rulings.court: Illinois Appellate Court, Fourth District; reviewing Calhoun County Circuit Court
rulings.judgeRole: Circuit judge who calculated the child-support obligation; not the appellate author.
rulings.holding: Burch set child support at $812.53 per month after allocating the payer's family health-insurance premium across the four children covered, two of whom were emancipated.
rulings.reasoning: He read the statute to require dividing the premium by the total number of people covered. The parties had agreed that the premium cost the same whether one or several children were insured.
rulings.subsequentHistory: The appellate court reversed and remanded on September 4, 2019. It held that the premium was available and verifiable, so the payer should receive credit for its full amount instead of a divided amount.

sbe-8th-circuit-retain-brenner-tad-brenn.name: Tad Brenner
sbe-8th-circuit-retain-brenner-tad-brenn.searchScope: Official Illinois Courts all-year index search for Tad Brenner; 16 full-text hits. Read final official Masters and Dyer opinions. The Masters caption confirms Talmadge 'Tad' Brenner's identity.

rulings.court: Illinois Appellate Court, Fourth District; reviewing Adams County Circuit Court
rulings.judgeRole: Circuit judge who denied postconviction relief following an evidentiary hearing. This profile does not attribute the original trial sentence to him.
rulings.holding: Brenner rejected an as-applied state constitutional challenge to a 115-year sentence for offenses committed at age 18.
rulings.reasoning: He found the developmental psychologist's testimony insufficiently tied to this defendant: it relied on unverified self-reports, conflicted with other records, and largely described young adults generally. He concluded the defendant had not established an individual constitutional violation.
rulings.subsequentHistory: The appellate court affirmed, finding no manifest error. Justice Knecht specially concurred in the judgment. The final official report dates filing December 3, 2024; the online index instead displays December 2, so the profile follows the final PDF.

evidence.title: Official Illinois Courts final opinion: People v. Masters

rulings.limitations: This was a fact-specific as-applied challenge, not a categorical ruling that every sentence for an 18-year-old is valid. Sentence severity and rejection of relief do not independently establish a partisan or Trump alignment.

policyComparison.reason: Individual proportional-sentencing claim outside the defined policy basket; no directly matched party or Trump proposition established.

rulings.court: Illinois Appellate Court, Fourth District; reviewing Adams County Circuit Court
rulings.judgeRole: Circuit judge who revoked release on December 7, 2023. Other judges handled earlier release orders; those actions are not attributed to Brenner.
rulings.holding: Brenner revoked release while a probation-revocation petition was pending after new charges were filed against the defendant.
rulings.reasoning: He found that the defendant had allegedly committed new qualifying offenses while released, and that no combination of conditions would ensure appearance or prevent further charges.
rulings.subsequentHistory: The appellate court vacated the order. The original probation petition did not allege a new criminal offense, so the release statute Brenner used did not authorize detention. The court remanded for consideration under the rules applicable to a later amended petition, permitting detention only if the proper statutory requirements were met.

rulings.limitations: The ruling concerned statutory detention eligibility in one probation case. It neither invalidated Illinois's cash-bail abolition nor expressed support for restoring money bail.

policyComparison.reason: Individual detention eligibility is different from the system-wide cash-bail policy proposition; no inferred support for Trump or either party.

sbe-9th-circuit-retain-vancil-jr-david-l.researchScope: Official Illinois Courts opinion index full-name search returned eight records; selected criminal-sentencing and family-law rulings inspected. The index does not cover all trial-court rulings.

rulings.court: Henderson County Circuit Court; reviewed by the Third District Appellate Court
rulings.judgeRole: Trial judge whose sentencing decision was reviewed; not an appellate panel member
rulings.holding: After revoking probation, Vancil imposed five years in prison and denied a request to consider credit for time already spent on probation.
rulings.reasoning: The trial court said Illinois had no provision allowing that credit. The appellate court held that the statute gave the judge discretion to consider it.
rulings.subsequentHistory: Reversed and remanded for the circuit court to consider whether to exercise that discretion. The appeal did not order that credit must be awarded; later proceedings were not established in this review.

rulings.dateMeaning: Appellate decision date; underlying plea and admonitions August 5, 2025
rulings.court: Knox County Circuit Court; reviewed by the Fourth District Appellate Court
rulings.judgeRole: Trial judge whose post-plea appeal-rights admonitions were reviewed
rulings.holding: Doyle accepted a negotiated guilty plea and three-year sentence, then provided a shortened oral explanation of appeal rights and a written form covering multiple types of proceedings.
rulings.reasoning: The court asked whether the defendant had signed the form and had questions, then explained the 30-day motion-to-withdraw requirement. The appellate court found the combined oral and written notices did not substantially convey the applicable Rule 605(c) rights.
rulings.subsequentHistory: The Fourth District remanded for proper Rule 605(c) admonitions. It did not decide that the defendant was innocent or that the firearm law was invalid. Later trial-court proceedings were not established in this review.

sbe-10th-circuit-retain-mack-james-a-mac.researchScope: Official Illinois Courts full-name search returned 52 records. Selected a published election-law decision; later Thomas litigation was excluded from this profile because that appealed ruling was by another judge.

rulings.caseName: Alms v. Peoria County Election Commission
rulings.dateMeaning: Appellate explanatory opinion date; preliminary appellate affirmance November 21, 2022; trial denial October 19, 2022
rulings.court: Peoria County Circuit Court; reviewed by the Fourth District Appellate Court
rulings.judgeRole: Trial judge who denied the preliminary injunction
rulings.topic: County referendum deadline, wording and certification
rulings.holding: Mack declined to block counting, canvassing and certification of a referendum to eliminate the county auditor's office.
rulings.reasoning: He read the 79-day statutory deadline as requiring adoption, not filing, of the referendum; the board had adopted it in time. He also found the challengers had not established the required likelihood of success and irreparable harm.
rulings.subsequentHistory: The Fourth District affirmed. It independently reviewed the legal questions, found the irreparable-harm argument forfeited and concluded the challengers had not shown a likelihood of success. The decision concerned preliminary relief, not a complete trial on every claim.

sbe-10th-circuit-retain-doscotch-christo.name: Christopher R. Doscotch
sbe-10th-circuit-retain-doscotch-christo.researchScope: Official Illinois Courts surname search returned 55 records. Selected two published cases on search-and-seizure/firearms and pretrial time limits, with the judge's role checked in the actual decisions.

rulings.dateMeaning: Appellate decision date; underlying suppression ruling March 2025 and constitutional motion May 2025
rulings.court: Tazewell County Circuit Court; reviewed by the Fourth District Appellate Court
rulings.judgeRole: Trial judge who denied suppression and a constitutional motion to dismiss
rulings.topic: Police searches and firearm possession after felony conviction
rulings.holding: Doscotch allowed a gun found in a passenger's backpack into evidence and rejected the defendant's as-applied Second Amendment challenge to the felon-in-possession statute. A stipulated bench trial resulted in a conviction.
rulings.reasoning: On suppression, he found the inventory search initially valid, discovery of suspected drugs supplied probable cause, and safety justified leaving the backpack in the car. The appellate opinion records denial of the constitutional motion but does not explain his separate constitutional reasoning.
rulings.subsequentHistory: The Fourth District affirmed both the suppression ruling and conviction, rejecting facial and as-applied firearm-law challenges. That appellate reasoning belongs to its panel, not automatically to Doscotch.

rulings.dateMeaning: Appellate decision date; release motions denied July 29 and August 1, 2024
rulings.court: Tazewell County Circuit Court; reviewed by the Fourth District Appellate Court
rulings.judgeRole: Trial judge who denied release under the statutory 90-day detention limit
rulings.holding: Doscotch denied a detained defendant's request for release based on expiration of the 90-day period for bringing a detained defendant to trial.
rulings.reasoning: He excluded an 11-day continuance connected with obtaining new defense counsel from that calculation. The issue was how continuances count under the statute, not the constitutionality of abolishing money bail.
rulings.subsequentHistory: The Fourth District affirmed on a different ground: a later defense-requested 14-day continuance tolled the clock even though it did not postpone the trial date. It expressly did not adopt the trial court's reasoning.
